fields.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
fields.note: The requirement summary matches the code: the at-fault and no-fault grounds, the notice contents, the relocation assistance, the right to re-rent within 5 years, the buyout rules, retaliation and the remedies. The code text sets out each of these.

fields.quoted_span: the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
fields.note: The 3-month amount for seniors and disabled tenants, the 15-day payment, the rent waiver, the 30/60-day notice, the 5-year re-rent right with 30 days to accept, the 3x damages and the 15-year exemption all appear in the code (§§ 98.0706(c), 98.0706(b), 98.0706(d), 98.0709(d)-(e), 98.0703(k)).

fields.quoted_span: (“Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy” added 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.)
fields.note: The effective date of 2023-06-24 and the enactment date of 2023-05-25 are confirmed. The amendment effective 3-28-2024 is also stated.
The text is the current 3-2024 code, with no repeal or sunset shown. The in_force status is consistent with the document.

fields.quoted_span: (k) housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome; and
fields.note: The tenancy definition (over 30 days, excluding fixed terms of 3 months or less), the owner-occupied exemptions, the hotel, short-term, MRL mobilehome and other listed exemptions, and the separately alienable property conditions all match the code text in §§ 98.0702-98.0703.

fields.quoted_span: §98.0704 Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
fields.note: § 98.0704 is the correct section. The aliases for ordinance numbers and for Division 7 (O-21647, O-21769, O-19269, §§ 98.0701-98.0710) are also confirmed in the document.
